speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin my assessment of this newborn, could you please describe the specific physical examination findings and the relevant history provided?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the lack of prenatal care and immunization records, I need to assess for potential congenital infections. Are there any specific physical findings such as hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, petechiae, or microcephaly noted on examination?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: These findings of congenital cataracts, sensorineural hearing loss, and a heart murmur are classic signs of congenital rubella syndrome, often referred to as the "blueberry muffin" rash. I will request specific serological testing to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Rubella IgM antibody test

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Rubella IgM confirms the diagnosis of congenital rubella syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome
